notes:
Background: Horizon Lynx is a mid-market SaaS company offering product analytics and contextual in-app guidance. Product org (Head of Product Jane Park) initiated evaluation to add an on-brand assistant + semantic search to the product. Started with Hosted API POC for speed-to-market; moved to Dedicated after performance and cost trade-offs surfaced.

POC & evaluation summary:
- Hosted API POC (Jan 2026): quick integration using embeddings + chat endpoints; good developer DX; cost unpredictable under synthetic traffic.
- Dedicated demo & 2-week staging POC (Feb 2026): ran on 2x A100-equivalent vGPUs in our staging; observed median tail-latency 80 ms for chat paths, 95th pct latency ~220 ms under synthetic 200 reqs/sec bursts.
- Throughput/volume: baseline production expected ~8k-12k requests/day, but seasonal marketing spikes and MLP testing can produce short-term bursts up to 3x baseline.
- Quality: prefer Llama 2 / open variants fine-tuned for instruction following; Redwood recommended quantized variant + caching for prompt prefixes.

Pricing / packaging negotiation (current):
- Customer preference: committed reserved capacity (monthly billing) with explicit ramp schedule rather than purely usage-based pricing. "We need predictability for budgeting and predictably priced bursts," J. Park.
- Proposed Redwood terms discussed: 12-month commitment with 3-step ramp: month1=2 reserved vGPUs, month4=4 reserved vGPUs, month7=6 reserved vGPUs; burst pool up to 2x reserved capacity for short windows.
- Overage / burst pricing: starting offer from Redwood was overage at 1.3x unit rate; Horizon requests a blended rate for bursts and a buffer of credits for onboarding month.
- Ramp & termination: Horizon asking for a 90-day opt-out window if SLAs not met in first 6 months; legal flagged by Redwood.
- Discounts: Horizon asking for commit discount scale (10% @ 12 mo / 18% @ 24 mo); Redwood AE countered with platform credits and Optimize consulting hours.

Security & compliance notes:
- SOC2 in-scope; must have SSO (SAML) + KMS integration for keys; audit log access required for first year. Data residency: US only for customer PII.
- Network: requires VPC peering / private egress and allowlisted IP ranges.

Salesplay & internal notes:
- AE Marcus Chen leading commercial negotiation; SE Ravi Patel driving technical POC benchmarks; CSM Elena Morris will pick up post-go-live.
- Key internal asks for Redwood: produce a ramped SOW showing vGPU units, burst rules, overage formula, and sample invoice for first 6 months. Provide SOC2 attestation and a short KMS integration runbook.

Customer quotes and tone:
- "We like the runtime performance in staging but can't be hostage to per-token spikes during product experiments." — Jane Park, Head of Product.
- "If Redwood can give a clear ramp + burst policy with predictable economics we can commit." — CFO (email 2026-02-28).

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to send draft SOW + pricing matrix by 2026-03-10.
- Legal exchange week of 2026-03-15.
- Technical sign-off POC 2 (load test with 4 reserved vGPUs) scheduled 2026-03-22.

Risks: budget committee may push for monthly vs annual billing; network peering lead time (4–6 weeks) could delay go-live.
